frontend/src/hooks/chapter/useChapterLoa.purpose: Chapter data fetch with timing instrumentation, segment freshness tracking, completion polling
notes: 2026-07-09: loadChapter() now calls api.fetchChapter(chapterId) (GET /api/chapters/{id}, ~700B/~4ms) instead of api.fetchChapters(projectId) + Array.find (GET /api/projects/{id}/chapters, ~780KB/~60-100ms for the measured 28-chapter book — the full list including every OTHER chapter's full text_content). This loader runs on mount, on every websocket chapter-update/segment-update tick, and on every 1s completion-poll tick (up to 30x per render), so the old code re-transferred the whole project's chapter text repeatedly just to read one chapter's fields. Minor behavior note: the single-chapter endpoint doesn't cross-check project_id the way `chapters.find(c => c.id === chapterId)` implicitly did — not exercised by real navigation (chapterId is always routing-scoped) so left as-is.

2026-07-10: Passes projectId to api.fetchChapter. On a 404 (error.status === 404) the catch block now clears chapter/segments/characters/scriptViewData and sets a new chapterNotFound flag instead of leaving stale state on screen with only a console.error.

frontend/src/hooks/useAnimatedSegmentPro.purpose: Per-segment-id animated interpolation lanes for the concurrent chapter-fanout map path

exports.name: useAnimatedSegmentProgress
exports.contract: activeSegmentsMap -> Record<segmentId, animatedProgress>; one independent ProgressLane per rendering-phase entry, anchored at each entry's latest real (progress, eta_seconds) and interpolated toward the ETA end-time between real frames; no positive eta -> lane holds (no fabricated motion); untouched entries left alone so a sibling's in-flight animation is never disturbed by another segment's frame

notes: Added 2026-07-06 to restore progress-presentation.md spec §7 H5 (text fill follows ANIMATED display progress, never raw stepped event data) for N concurrently-rendering segments -- reuses the bar's existing lane math and 250ms tickMs cadence rather than inventing new interpolation logic. One shared setInterval keyed on a boolean so frame-identity churn never resets the timer.
